findings.evidence: Page 148, Table 7-2: Fine-tuning Adam row states "~1,120 GB" with bytes per param "~16 B/param total (FP16 weights + gradients + FP32 master copy + Adam m + v)". Check: 16 × 70B = 1,120B bytes = 1,120 GB ✓. Decomposition: weights 2B + gradients 2B + FP32 master 4B + Adam m 4B + v 4B = 16B/param ✓. And the row says "fits 8×H100: no" — check: 1,120 GB > 640 GB ✓. But the page 149 note says "roughly 1.75× the 640 GB of 8×H100 (1,120 ÷ 640)" — check: 1120/640 = 1.75 ✓. However the same note also says "§7.6 states the same gap as ≈6.8× against the ~164 GB inference residency floor" — check: 1120/164.1 = 6.825... ≈ 6.8× ✓. Both multiples correct with stated denominators ✓.
findings.issue: No arithmetic defect — fine-tuning memory floor and its multiples against both denominators recompute correctly.

findings.evidence: Page 151, §7.3.3 quantization section: MXFP4 rate stated as "17 bytes per 32 values, or 0.53125 B/value". Check: 17/32 = 0.53125 ✓. NVFP4 stated as "18 bytes per 32 values, or 0.5625 B/value". Check: 18/32 = 0.5625 ✓. Also "MXFP4 adds one local-scale byte" and "one E8M0 scale shared by a block of 32 values" — consistent with the OCP MX spec description ✓. Page 153 worked example: MXFP4 for 16,777,216 values = 8,912,896 bytes. Check: 16,777,216 × 0.53125 = 8,912,896 ✓. NVFP4: 16,777,216 × 0.5625 + 4 = 9,437,188 + 4 = 9,437,192? Wait — 16,777,216 × 0.5625 = 9,437,184. Plus 4 bytes global scale = 9,437,188 ✓. All correct.
findings.issue: No arithmetic defect — quantization byte accounting for MXFP4 and NVFP4 recompute correctly including the global-scale term.

findings.evidence: Page 146, §7.3.2: "With BF16 KV storage, the raw component is: 2 × 16 × 4 × 256 × 2 = 65,536 bytes per cached token." Check: 2 × 16 × 4 × 256 × 2 = 65,536 ✓. "At 262,144 cached tokens, this component occupies 16 GiB (17,179,869,184 B ≈ 17.18 GB on the chapter's decimal GB basis, §7.1)". Check: 262,144 × 65,536 = 17,179,869,184 B ✓. 17,179,869,184 B / 10⁹ = 17.18 GB ✓. 16 GiB = 16 × 2³⁰ = 17,179,869,184 ✓. "At 131,072 tokens the same component is 8 GiB (8,589,934,592 B ≈ 8.59 GB decimal)". Check: 131,072 × 65,536 = 8,589,934,592 ✓; /10⁹ = 8.59 GB ✓. "Doubling history therefore adds 8 GiB (≈8.59 GB decimal)". Check: 16 − 8 = 8 GiB ✓; 17.18 − 8.59 = 8.59 ✓. All correct.
findings.issue: No arithmetic defect — Qwen3.8-27B full-attention KV component arithmetic recompute correctly on both GiB and GB bases.

findings.evidence: Page 154, INT4 worked example: "an illustrative INT4 layout containing an FP16 scale and a packed four-bit zero point per group uses 8,716,288 bytes for the same matrix" (4096 × 4096 = 16,777,216 values, groups of 128). Check: 16,777,216 values / 128 per group = 131,072 groups. Per group: 128 values × 4 bits = 512 bits = 64 bytes payload; plus FP16 scale = 2 bytes; plus packed 4-bit zero = 0.5 bytes. Total per group: 64 + 2 + 0.5 = 66.5 bytes. Total: 131,072 × 66.5 = 8,716,288 bytes ✓. Then "Replacing the packed zero with an FP16 scaled-zero increases that layout to 8,912,896 bytes". Check: per group: 64 + 2 + 2 = 68 bytes; 131,072 × 68 = 8,912,896 ✓. "Only the FP16 scaled-zero variant (8,912,896 bytes) matches MXFP4's total". Check: MXFP4 was also 8,912,896 ✓. "That match is a coincidence of layout rates rather than a shared design: 4 metadata bytes per 128-value group (2 B scale + 2 B zero) and MXFP4's 1 scale byte per 32-value group both come to 0.03125 B/value on top of the same four-bit payload." Check: 4/128 = 0.03125; 1/32 = 0.03125 ✓. All correct.
findings.issue: No arithmetic defect — INT4 vs MXFP4 byte accounting recompute correctly including the coincidence observation.
